mainTopic: The end of the pecked-dough sugya, and the משנה and גמרא on the laws of יחוד (seclusion)
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a ברייתא about dough that chickens may have pecked after drinking טמא liquid. רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן then argue over which liquids leave the dough in doubt. A new משנה begins on יחוד: a man may not be alone with two women, but one woman may be alone with two men. רבי שמעון permits it when the man's wife is with him, and there are special rules for a mother and a daughter. The גמרא explains the reason for the rule and finds a hint for יחוד in the פסוק about a מסית, 'your brother, the son of your mother.' It then discusses whether אבא שאול disagrees with the משנה, and the argument over whether mourning breaks a person's יצר. Finally רב limits the היתר of two men to decent men, and the גמרא brings proofs. The last proof, from the סוטה escorts, is being rejected, and that answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Pecked dough stays in doubt
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if there are peck marks in the dough, its status is held in doubt. It is neither eaten nor burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are little peck marks in the dough, it is held in doubt: we do not eat it and we do not burn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא, begun on the previous עמוד, about chickens that may have drunk טמא liquid and then pecked at the dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know whether the chickens drank the טמא liquid before they pecked. So the dough is not declared clearly טמא (which would mean burning it) and not clearly טהור (which would mean eating it). It stays תלויה (in doubt). This doubtful ruling supports רבי יוחנן's view in the earlier case of the child.

keyTerms.meaning: Peck marks, small holes made by a bird's beak
We leave it in doubt (it stays in suspension)
We burn it (what is done with definitely טמא תרומה)

phrases.english: If there are peck marks in the dough —
it is held in doubt; it is not eaten and it is not burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא brought on the previous עמוד in support of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that in such cases the dough stays a matter of doubt
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the ברייתא about chickens pecking at dough

steps.title: Only white liquids leave doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי limits the ruling to white liquids. With red liquids, the pecks would leave visible red marks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: This ruling was taught only about white liquids. With red liquids, if the chickens had pecked after drinking, we would clearly see it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי narrows the ברייתא's ruling of doubt to one case only: white liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White liquid leaves no visible trace on dough, so we cannot tell whether the chickens drank it first. Red liquid would stain the peck marks, so we could check. No red marks would mean no doubt at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
They taught this only with white liquids,
but with red liquids —
if it were so that they had pecked,
it would surely be known.
phrases.notes: He means the peck marks would show red from the liquid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling of doubt applies only to white liquid. With red liquid, the marks would show.

steps.title: Maybe the dough soaked it up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי: maybe the dough absorbed the red liquid, so no mark would show.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the dough absorbed the liquid, and that is why there is no mark?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reasoning of רבי יהושע בן לוי from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic depends on red liquid always leaving a visible mark. But dough can soak in liquid, and then even red liquid might leave no trace. If so, no marks does not prove there were no pecks, and the doubt comes back.

phrases.english: But perhaps the dough absorbed them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's distinction between white and red liquids
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Color does not guarantee a mark, because dough may absorb the liquid completely.

steps.title: Clear versus murky liquids
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי יהושע בן לוי heard the ruling without its explanation. The real line is clear liquid versus murky liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The distinguished one heard this ruling but did not hear its explanation. It was taught only about clear liquids, the kind where a child can see his reflection. But murky liquids are not included.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן fixes the distinction so that it answers the challenge from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clear liquid can sink into dough without leaving a trace, so the doubt is real. Murky liquid would leave a stain, so we could tell whether the chickens pecked. The test is clearness, not color.

keyTerms.meaning: The distinguished one, a title of honor (here for רבי יהושע בן לוי)

steps.whatToRemember: The dough stays in doubt only with clear liquid, which can soak in without a trace. Murky liquid would leave a mark, so there is no doubt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The distinguished one heard this matter,
phrases.notes: "The distinguished one" is a respectful way of referring to רבי יהושע בן לוי.

phrases.english: but he did not hear its explanation:
They taught this only with clear liquids,
in which a child's reflection can be seen,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the letter in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: but murky liquids — not.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר זֶה שָׁמַע בְּרִיבִּי וּפֵירוּשׁוֹ לֹא שָׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3 by changing what the distinction is based on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the distinction (clear versus murky, instead of white versus red)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Color decides whether a mark would show.
steps.terutzMaskana: Clearness decides it: clear liquid can be absorbed without a trace, while murky liquid leaves a mark.

steps.title: Basic rule of seclusion
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a man may not be alone with two women, but one woman may be alone with two men.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man may not be alone with two women. But one woman may be alone with two men.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: the laws of יחוד (seclusion).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not symmetrical. Two women do not prevent a man from being considered alone with them. Two men with one woman are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the rule works the same in both directions. Two women with one man is forbidden, but two men with one woman is allowed.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִתְיַיחֵד אָדָם עִם שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים,
phrases.english: A man may not be secluded with two women,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִשָּׁה אַחַת מִתְיַיחֶדֶת עִם שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים.
phrases.english: but one woman may be secluded with two men.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יִתְיַיחֵד אָדָם עִם שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic; begins a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One man with two women is forbidden. One woman with two men is permitted.

steps.title: When his wife is with him
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון permits a man to be alone with two women, and even sleep in the same inn, when his own wife is with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Even one man may be alone with two women when his wife is with him, and he may sleep with them in an inn, because his wife watches over him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds an exception to the first rule of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern in step 5 is that the man might sin. His wife being present acts as a guard against that, so the prohibition does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: When his wife is with him

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף אִישׁ אֶחָד מִתְיַיחֵד עִם שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
phrases.english: Even one man may be secluded with two women
when his wife is with him,
and he may sleep with them in an inn,
because his wife guards him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר אַף אִישׁ אֶחָד מִתְיַיחֵד עִם שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the first rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When his wife is present, a man may be alone with two women, because she guards him.

steps.title: Mother and daughter
steps.stepSummary: A man may be alone with his mother and his daughter and even sleep close to them. Once they are grown, each sleeps in their own garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man may be alone with his mother and with his daughter, and sleep with them with bodily contact. Once they have grown up, she sleeps in her garment and he sleeps in his garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets the rules of יחוד for close relatives: a man with his mother and his daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With these close relatives, being alone together is permitted, and even sleeping with bodily contact. Once they have grown up, there is a limit: each must sleep in their own garment.
steps.whatToRemember: The יחוד rules in this משנה: no man with two women (unless his wife is there, according to רבי שמעון); one woman with two men is allowed; with mother and daughter even sleeping close is allowed, but once they are grown each sleeps in their own garment.

phrases.aramaic: מִתְיַיחֵד אָדָם עִם אִמּוֹ וְעִם בִּתּוֹ
phrases.english: A man may be secluded with his mother and with his daughter
and sleep with them with bodily contact.
And if they have grown up —
this one sleeps in her garment
and that one sleeps in his garment.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתְיַיחֵד אָדָם עִם אִמּוֹ וְעִם בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the case of close relatives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יחוד with one's mother and daughter is permitted, even sleeping with bodily contact. Once they are grown, each sleeps in their own garment.

steps.title: Why is the rule different for men and women?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's rule: a man may not be alone with two women, but a woman may be alone with two men.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה treats the two cases differently. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 5) said two women are not enough to stop a man, but two men are enough to make it okay for one woman. The גמרא wants the logic behind this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Being alone together with someone in a private place

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He's asking about the משנה's rule: why can't two women protect a man, when two men can protect one woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's rule about יחוד (step 5) to ask for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind the difference between a man with two women and a woman with two men.

steps.title: Because women are more easily swayed
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי אליהו explains that women are more easily persuaded, so two women do not stop each other the way two men would.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of אליהו taught: since women are of light mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question using a teaching from תנא דבי אליהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that women are more easily persuaded. So the presence of a second woman does not protect well enough, while two men hold each other back. This explains why the משנה's rule is lopsided.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school (collection) of אליהו
Their minds are 'light', meaning more easily swayed

phrases.english: The school of Eliyahu taught:
Since women are of light mind.
phrases.notes: He means they are more easily talked into things, so a second woman won't stop it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Women are more easily persuaded, so two women do not protect a man, but two men do protect a woman.

steps.title: Where does the Torah hint at יחוד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the prohibition of יחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks where the whole idea of a יחוד prohibition comes from. This sets up the source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 explained one detail, why two women aren't enough. Now the גמרא goes back to the bigger question: what is the basis for forbidding יחוד at all?

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason for a detail to the source of the whole prohibition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source for the prohibition of יחוד.

steps.title: The hint: 'your brother, the son of your mother'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes רבי ישמעאל, who finds a hint for יחוד in the פסוק about one who tempts others to worship idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: From where is there a hint in the Torah to יחוד? As it says: 'If your brother, the son of your mother, entices you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the source by quoting רבי ישמעאל. He points to a פסוק about a מסית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice he calls it only a רמז, a hint, not a full Torah source. The פסוק is about idol worship, and the hint comes from the odd words 'son of your mother.' The next step explains how.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint (not a full, direct source)
Someone who tempts others to worship idols

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
From where is there a hint in the Torah to seclusion?
As it is stated: “If your brother, the son of your mother, entices you.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 by naming a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'כי יסיתך אחיך בן אמך' hints at יחוד.

steps.title: How the פסוק teaches about יחוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל asks why the פסוק says 'son of your mother' and explains: a son may be alone with his mother, so brothers through the mother grow close. This implies being alone with other עריות is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only a son of the mother who entices, and a son of the father does not? Rather, it is to tell you: a son may be alone with his mother, and it is forbidden to be alone with all the עריות of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל shows how the hint works. He points out that the words 'son of your mother' seem unnecessary, and draws a lesson from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother from the father can entice just as well, so why mention the mother? Because a son may be alone with his mother, so her sons from different husbands spend time together and become close. A son does not do that with his father's other wife, since she is an ערוה, which shows that יחוד with עריות is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Relatives the Torah forbids one to marry or be with

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'is it only a mother's son who entices?' is not a real challenge to the פסוק. It is רבי ישמעאל pointing out a strange word so he can learn something from it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main Torah hint for the whole איסור of יחוד, and also the source that a son may be alone with his mother.

phrases.english: But is it only the son of a mother who entices,
and the son of a father does not entice?
Rather, it is to tell you:
A son may be alone with his mother,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָסוּר לְהִתְיַיחֵד עִם כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and it is forbidden to be alone with all those forbidden relations of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי בֶּן אֵם מֵסִית, בֶּן אָב אֵינוֹ מֵסִית? אֶלָּא לוֹמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק of step 11 hints at יחוד.
steps.raayaObject: That יחוד with עריות is forbidden, while a son may be alone with his mother.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words 'בן אמך' in the פסוק of the מסית.

steps.title: What does the פסוק mean in its own setting?
steps.stepSummary: Since 'son of your mother' was only a hint, the גמרא asks what those words mean in the plain sense of the פסוק about idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: The plain meaning of the פסוק, what is it written about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the words 'son of your mother' mean in the simple reading. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hint does not erase the פסוק's simple meaning. The פסוק is about a מסית, so the גמרא wants to know why, in that setting, it speaks of a mother's son.

keyTerms.meaning: The plain, simple meaning of the פסוק

phrases.english: With regard to what is the plain meaning of the verse written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After using the פסוק as a hint, asks about its simple meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק of the מסית mentions specifically a mother's son, in its plain sense.

steps.title: אביי: even a friendly brother must not be listened to
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the פסוק uses a 'not only this, but even that' style: a father's son, who resents you, obviously shouldn't be trusted, but even a mother's son, who is friendly, must not be listened to.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It speaks in the style of 'it is not needed.' It is not needed to say a son of the father, who hates him and gives him bad advice. But even a son of the mother, who doesn't hate him, you might say he should listen to him. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question: the פסוק picks the harder case to teach a bigger point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother through the father competes with you for the same inheritance, so he may hate you and give bad advice. A brother through the mother inherits from a different father, so he has no reason to hate you, and you might trust him. The פסוק says: even him, do not listen to when he tempts you to idol worship.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed to say (the obvious case); 'not only this, but even that'

steps.whatToRemember: The words 'בן אמך' do two jobs: as a hint, they teach about יחוד (a son may be alone with his mother; other עריות are forbidden), and in the plain meaning, they teach that you must not listen to a מסית even when he is a loving brother.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary.'
It is not necessary to say the son of a father,

phrases.aramaic: דְּסָנֵי לֵיהּ וְעָיֵיץ לֵיהּ עֵצוֹת רָעוֹת,
phrases.english: who hates him and gives him bad advice,
but even the son of a mother,
who does not hate him,
you might say he should listen to him,
so it teaches us that he should not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 about the plain meaning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק uses a 'not only, but even' style: even a friendly brother through the mother must not be listened to when he tempts you to idol worship.

steps.title: Does our משנה go against אבא שאול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה, which forbids a man to be alone with two women, disagrees with אבא שאול. In a ברייתא about burying a baby, he allows one man with two women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow אבא שאול? A ברייתא teaches: a baby who dies within thirty days is carried out in someone's arms. He is buried by one woman and two men, but not by one man and two women. אבא שאול says: even by one man and two women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where אבא שאול seems to allow one man to be alone with two women. That seems to clash with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a man may not be alone with two women. In the ברייתא, the תנא קמא agrees and forbids one man with two women at a baby's burial. אבא שאול permits it, so it looks like the משנה is against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
in the bosom, carried in someone's arms instead of on a bier
a תנא who argues with the תנא קמא here
a man and a woman being alone together in a forbidden way

phrases.english: Shall we say our משנה is not like אבא שאול,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
all thirty days, he is carried out in the bosom,
phrases.notes: This is a baby who died within his first thirty days.

phrases.english: and is buried by one woman and two men,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא בְּאִישׁ אֶחָד וּשְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים.
phrases.english: but not by one man and two women.
אבא שאול says:
even by one man and two women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the משנה's rule about one man with two women and checks it against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a man may not be alone with two women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אבא שאול allows one man with two women at a burial, so the משנה seems to go against his view.

steps.title: Mourning breaks a person's desire
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can follow אבא שאול. He allows it only during fresh mourning, when the desire to sin is broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows אבא שאול. At a time of fresh mourning, a person's desire is broken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אבא שאול agrees with the משנה in normal cases. He is lenient only at a burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול's leniency is not a general permission to be alone with two women. It is an exception for the time of אנינות, when grief takes away the urge to sin. So the משנה and אבא שאול do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: you can even say (it fits this opinion too)
fresh mourning, right after a close relative dies

steps.confusionAlert: אבא שאול does not argue on the basic איסור יחוד. He makes an exception only for the special time of mourning.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows אבא שאול:
at a time of fresh mourning, his inclination is broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the leniency applies only to mourning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אבא שאול allows a man to be alone with two women in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: He allows it only during אנינות, because then the יצר is broken.

steps.title: The רבנן follow רבי יצחק: the יצר is strong even in mourning
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן forbid it even at a burial. רבי יצחק reads a פסוק in איכה to teach that the יצר overpowers a person even while he is mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold like רבי יצחק. רבי יצחק said: "Why does a living man complain, a man over his sins?" Even at a person's time of fresh mourning, his inclination overpowers him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן disagree with אבא שאול. It brings a פסוק as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק reads 'יתאונן' as connected to אונן, a mourner. He reads 'גבר' as 'overpowering.' So the פסוק teaches that even a mourner's sins can overpower him, and the רבנן do not trust grief to prevent יחוד.

keyTerms.meaning: complain; here read as being an אונן (mourner)

phrases.english: And the רבנן hold like רבי יצחק.
For רבי יצחק said:
"Why does a living man complain,
a man over his sins":
even at the time of a person's fresh mourning,
phrases.notes: He hears 'יתאונן' as being an אונן, a mourner.

phrases.english: his inclination overpowers him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining אבא שאול, the גמרא explains the רבנן.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's view that one man may not be with two women even during mourning.

steps.title: How does אבא שאול read that פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what אבא שאול does with רבי יצחק's פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אבא שאול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how אבא שאול explains the פסוק. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק teaches that a mourner's יצר is still strong, אבא שאול's leniency seems wrong. So the גמרא needs to know how he reads it.

phrases.english: And אבא שאול?
phrases.notes: Meaning: what does he do with this פסוק?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions אבא שאול in light of the פסוק brought in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How אבא שאול explains איכה 3:39 so that it does not go against him.

steps.title: The פסוק is about complaining against ה׳
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול reads the פסוק as talking about a person who complains about how ה׳ treats him. It is not about mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק was written about one who complains about ה׳'s ways. This is what it says: why should he complain about His ways? Has he overcome his sins? The life I gave him is enough for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives אבא שאול's reading of the פסוק. With this reading, it says nothing about mourners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אבא שאול, 'יתאונן' means complaining, and 'גבר על חטאיו' is a question: has he beaten his sins? ה׳ answers that being alive is already enough of a gift. So the פסוק gives no proof against his leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: His ways (how ה׳ deals with people)

phrases.english: When that was written,
it was written about one who complains about His ways,
and this is what it is saying:
why should he complain about His ways?
Has he then overcome his sins?
The life I gave him is enough for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי כְּתִיב הָהוּא בְּמִתְרַעֵם עַל מִדּוֹתָיו כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אבא שאול reads the פסוק as being about someone who complains against ה׳, not about a mourner's יצר.

steps.title: The story of the woman who sinned while mourning
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן point to a known story of a woman who sinned while mourning and even took her husband out of his grave. It shows the יצר is strong even in grief.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They point to that incident with a certain woman, where there was an incident and she took him out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the רבנן with a real-life story. It shows a mourner can still give in to temptation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול's reason was that grief breaks desire. The story shows the opposite: a widow in fresh mourning sinned and even took out her husband's body from the grave. So the רבנן do not rely on mourning to prevent sin.
steps.whatToRemember: אבא שאול allows one man with two women only during אנינות, because grief breaks the יצר. The רבנן forbid it even then, based on רבי יצחק's פסוק and the story of the widow. Both agree to the basic איסור יחוד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that sadness or a serious setting does not make the rules of יחוד go away. The יצר can be strong even in hard moments.

phrases.english: And the רבנן?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why do the רבנן insist that the יצר is still strong in mourning?

phrases.english: Like that incident
of that certain woman,
where there was an incident and she took him out.
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes we know the story. A widow sinned at her husband's grave and then took his body out of the grave.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן כִּי הָהוּא מַעֲשֶׂה דְּהַהִיא אִיתְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אבא שאול took away the proof from the פסוק, the רבנן support their view with a real event.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's view that the יצר is strong even during אנינות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the widow who sinned while mourning and took her husband out of his grave.

steps.title: רב limits the rule to decent men
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that one woman may be alone with two men. רב says this is only true for decent men. With immoral men, even ten men do not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one woman may be alone with two men. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: this was only taught about decent men. With immoral men, she may not be alone even with ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה and brings רב's limit on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed one woman to be with two men, since each man is embarrassed in front of the other. רב says this only works with decent men, who feel that shame. Immoral men do not feel it, so even a big group does not protect her.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about... (a phrase that limits a rule)
Men who are loose in their morals

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key limit on the היתר of being alone with two men. Whether it works depends on the kind of people involved, not only on how many there are.

phrases.english: But one woman
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: one woman may be alone with two men.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
They taught this only about decent men,
but with immoral men,
even with ten she may also not be alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּכְשֵׁרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of mourning to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may be alone with two men only if they are decent. With immoral men, even ten are not enough.

steps.title: A story where ten men sinned together
steps.stepSummary: There was a real case where ten men carried a woman out on a bier and sinned with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident, and ten men carried her out on a bier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב with a real event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that even ten immoral men are not safe. This story shows it actually happened: ten men worked together to sin, so a large group gave no protection.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a bier used to carry the dead

phrases.english: There was an incident,
and ten men carried her out on a bier.
phrases.notes: They carried her out as if she were dead, and then sinned with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's statement with a real event.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that even ten immoral men are not safe
steps.raayaSupportSource: A known incident of ten men carrying out a woman on a bier

steps.title: רב יוסף: groups can sin without shame
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף shows from everyday life that ten people can team up to steal a beam and not feel ashamed in front of each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: You can see that this is true, because ten people join together to steal a beam, and they are not ashamed in front of one another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a common-sense proof for רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea behind 'two men are fine' is that each man is ashamed in front of the other. רב יוסף points out that people in a group can do wrong together without any shame. So the same can happen with immoral men and a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Know it / you can see that this is true (opens a proof)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Know that this is true,
since ten people join together
and steal a beam,
and they are not ashamed in front of one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a reasoning proof on top of the story.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a group of immoral men gives no protection
steps.raayaSupportSource: The everyday fact that groups steal together without shame

steps.title: A suggested proof from the סוטה escorts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה in סוטה supports רב. It sends two תלמידי חכמים with the husband, which seems to show that ordinary men would not be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? The משנה says: they give him two תלמידי חכמים, in case he has relations with her on the way. This implies תלמידי חכמים, yes, but ordinary people, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to find support for רב in another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband takes his wife, a סוטה, to the מקדש, and she is forbidden to him until then. The משנה insists the escorts be תלמידי חכמים. This seems to show that ordinary men are not trusted to stop sin, which fits רב's view that not every pair of men protects.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
They give him two Torah scholars,
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה in סוטה, about a husband bringing his suspected wife to the מקדש.

phrases.english: in case he has relations with her on the way.
Torah scholars, yes;
ordinary people, no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a third support for רב, this time from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that not every pair of men gives protection
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוטה that requires two תלמידי חכמים as escorts

steps.title: Torah scholars are different because they know
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof. It says תלמידי חכמים are needed for a different reason, because of something they know.
steps.simpleTranslation: תלמידי חכמים are different, because they know...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested proof from the סוטה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed ordinary men were left out because they cannot be trusted. The גמרא answers that תלמידי חכמים are chosen for a special skill they have. So the משנה says nothing about whether ordinary men protect, and the full reason continues on the next עמוד.
steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Wait for the next lines to see what the scholars 'know' before deciding what the answer means.

phrases.english: Torah scholars are different, because they know

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the סוטה escorts, not רב's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תלמידי חכמים are chosen for a special reason (what they know), not because ordinary men are untrustworthy.
